name: Connecticut

sales.rateNote: Single statewide rate of 6.35%; no city or county sales taxes. Special rates apply to meals (7.35%), luxury items (7.75%), short-term car rentals (9.35%), vessels (2.99%) and business computer services (1%).

local.levies: none: no additional sales taxes are imposed by local jurisdictions

groceries.note: Food products for human consumption are exempt; meals and certain beverages are taxed at 7.35%.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxed at 6.35%; items over $1,000 are taxed at the 7.75% luxury rate. During Sales Tax Free Week, clothing and footwear under $300 per item are exempt.

otherRates.item: luxury goods: most motor vehicles over $50,000, jewelry over $5,000, clothing, footwear, handbags, luggage, umbrellas, wallets or watches over $1,000
otherRates.note: Luxury rate on the full sales price.

otherRates.item: passenger vehicle rental or lease of 30 days or less
vessels, vessel motors and vessel trailers
computer and data processing services; canned software for business use delivered electronically
motor vehicle sold to nonresident active-duty military stationed in Connecticut

holidays2026.name: Sales Tax Free Week
holidays2026.items: Most clothing and footwear costing less than $300 per item, in stores and online (limit raised from $100; cleated shoes and backpacks now included).

sales.holidayNote: 2026 was Connecticut's 27th Sales Tax Free Week.

useTax.note: Use tax rates are identical to the sales tax rates and apply to goods and taxable services bought for use in Connecticut without Connecticut tax.

facts.text: Connecticut has no local sales taxes: the 6.35% rate is the same in every town.
A 7.75% luxury rate applies to cars over $50,000, jewelry over $5,000 and clothing, handbags or watches over $1,000.
Sales Tax Free Week 2026 ran August 16-22 and covered clothing and footwear under $300 per item, up from $100.
Nonelectronic school supplies such as pens, pencils, notebooks, binders and rulers bought for non-business use are exempt year-round under Conn. Gen. Stat. 12-412(128).
Retailers may not advertise that they will pay or absorb the sales tax; violations carry a $500 fine per offense.
Meals are taxed at 7.35%, one point above the general rate.

property.levied: Local only: each town or city (and some fire and special districts) assesses and levies property tax on real estate, business personal property and motor vehicles; Connecticut has no state property tax levy.

assessment.text: Municipalities assess all property at a uniform 70% of present true and actual value (Conn. Gen. Stat. 12-62a). Towns must carry out a revaluation at least every five years under a schedule set by the Office of Policy and Management.

homestead.name: No general homestead exemption
homestead.text: Connecticut has no statewide homestead exemption for all homeowners. Relief is targeted: the state Elderly and Totally Disabled Homeowners program (circuit breaker) reduces the tax of eligible low-income owners by up to $1,250 (married) or $1,000 (unmarried), and towns may offer local options.
homestead.applyBy: Apply to the local assessor; income limits are indexed each year by OPM.

otherRelief.name: Elderly and Totally Disabled Homeowners Tax Relief
otherRelief.text: Owners aged 65+ or totally disabled with qualifying income under the indexed limits receive a property tax reduction of 10% to 50% of their tax, up to $1,250 for married owners.

otherRelief.name: Motor vehicle mill rate cap
otherRelief.text: Towns may not tax motor vehicles above 32.46 mills; since July 1, 2025 they may set a lower vehicle mill rate, down to zero.

dueDates.text: Due dates are set by each municipality. An installment becomes delinquent if not paid by the same day of the following month (one-month grace period); delinquent tax bears interest at 18% a year (1.5% per month).

facts.text: Cars are subject to local property tax in Connecticut, but the motor vehicle mill rate is capped at 32.46 mills.
All property is assessed at 70% of market value, so a $400,000 home has a $280,000 assessment before the town's mill rate is applied.
Since October 1, 2023, towns revalue on a schedule set by OPM for each revaluation zone, at least every five years.
Late property tax accrues 18% annual interest, with each part of a month counted as a full month.
Connecticut assessment years start on October 1, and revaluations take effect on an October 1 assessment date.
